quotes.quote: No, no, I didn't tell anybody. As far as family and friends were concerned, it was business as usual this whole time. I explained away his behavior to everybody.

persons.decisive_work_quote: Ultimately, he was convicted of felony arson, breaking an entering and vandalism for all of that.
persons.time_to_first_effective_action: same day as the son's abduction, after police had come 8-10 times
persons.name: Amelia (ex-husband)
persons.harm: Escalating harassment, stalking of her phone, night-time threats and intimidation, a push and a thrown object, a gun-store death threat, abduction of their son for extortion, and arson of the family home by her ex-husband during their divorce.
persons.perpetrator_role: her ex-husband

contacts.when: after the chainsaw incident, on attorney's advice; repeated calls
contacts.what_was_asked: stop the night-time harassment and threats
contacts.what_institution_did: Came out repeatedly but said nothing could be done until he physically assaulted her.
contacts.quote: The police would come and they would say until he physically assaults you, there's nothing we can do.
contacts.what_happened_next: Harassment continued; she kept calling (police came 8-10 times in total).
contacts.notes: She says the cops had been to the house 'like eight or 10 times' before the restraining order.

contacts.when: after he pushed her against a wall and threw a toy at her face
contacts.what_institution_did: Said it sounded like assault but without visible marks they could do nothing.
contacts.quote: I called the police and told them what happened. They said it sounds like assault but we don't see any physical marks so we can't do anything.
contacts.what_happened_next: No action; she notes no videos or texts were 'enough'.

contacts.what_was_asked: remove him from the account / stop him tracking her phone
contacts.what_institution_did: Security worked on the line to cut off his phone but he kept restoring service.
contacts.quote: they said this guy is good. We don't know how he's getting through all these walls, we keep shutting his phone off and he keeps turning it back on
contacts.what_happened_next: He texted her from the still-working phone with a gun-store location threat.

contacts.what_was_asked: protection after a threat to kill
contacts.what_institution_did: Deputies held him outside while she collected belongings; when shown a shrine with her photos and defaced journal they said they could do nothing.
contacts.quote: And he said, oh, it's definitely crazy, but crazy is not illegal. We can't do anything.
contacts.what_happened_next: She left to stay at a friend's house.
contacts.notes: Escort while she retrieved belongings is the concrete step; no action on the threat or shrine.

contacts.when: the morning he came to her workplace
contacts.what_was_asked: call her if he shows up to take the children
contacts.what_institution_did: The director was about to call her when he arrived and took their oldest son.
contacts.quote: I go inside, the director of the daycare has the phone in her handage that I was just about to call you.
contacts.what_happened_next: He drove off with the boy unrestrained.

contacts.institution: local police (called first by her work security)
contacts.when: the day he took their son
contacts.what_was_asked: find her son; respond to extortion threat
contacts.what_institution_did: Police spoke with her at work, dispatched a helicopter after the abduction/extortion call and told her to get a restraining order.
contacts.quote: I told that to the police and they dispatched a helicopter to try to find the car.
contacts.what_happened_next: Officer told her to go to the courthouse for a restraining order; the father brought the boy home around midnight.
contacts.notes: Work security called police initially because of how his car was parked.

contacts.what_institution_did: Clerk identified it as domestic violence; judge granted an order requiring him to leave the house immediately.
contacts.quote: And I explained everything that was going on and she looks at me and she said, that's domestic violence.
contacts.what_happened_next: Order granted ('he has to leave the house immediately') but not yet served.

contacts.what_institution_did: Two deputies served the order on the spot, removed him and warned he would go to jail if he returned.
contacts.quote: The sheriff looked at him and said, more making this real clear. If you show up here again, you're going to jail.
contacts.what_happened_next: He left; days later a deputy told her he had been arrested for DUI and tested positive for methamphetamine.
contacts.notes: She had first been told officers would not serve restraining orders.

contacts.when: a couple of days after service
contacts.what_institution_did: Judge kept him away from the home but allowed visitation monitored by his mother; she then dropped the order with that stipulation.
contacts.quote: The judge basically said that he still had to stay away from the home and he was still not allowed in our residence,
contacts.what_happened_next: Three days later he broke in and set the house on fire.

contacts.what_was_asked: emergency response (911 calls by his mother and neighbours)
contacts.what_institution_did: SWAT and a hostage negotiator besieged the house for six hours until he surrendered; he was taken to hospital and then jail; she got an emergency protective order.
contacts.quote: A few hours later, finally he surrendered. The SWAT team went inside and brought him out.
contacts.what_happened_next: Emergency protective order from the sheriffs; registered for custody-status notifications.

contacts.what_institution_did: Called her (and her friend) at midnight when he was released on bail.
contacts.quote: it's that registry calling both of us saying that the status of the inmate has changed and he is out on bail.
contacts.what_happened_next: Mental-health colleagues urged her to go into hiding.

contacts.what_institution_did: Police escorted her to a women's shelter; she left after two days because it was not a place she wanted her boys.
contacts.quote: So I packed up the room and we went to a women's shelter. You follow the police car and they take you to the women's shelter.
contacts.what_happened_next: Returned to a hotel under an alias.

contacts.institution: police department of the city where she was staying (detective)
contacts.what_was_asked: threat assessment requested by his former employer
contacts.what_institution_did: Detective ran a threat assessment and added extra patrols around her hotel.
contacts.quote: the detective said, we're going to do some extra patrols around the hotel you're staying in to make sure that you're safe.
contacts.what_happened_next: She felt 'a little bit of solace'.

contacts.what_institution_did: Told her to take time off.
contacts.quote: My work was wonderful. My work said take some time off, get your feet back under you, we're fine here.

contacts.what_institution_did: Initially warned it might not cover owner arson, housed them in a hotel, then covered 100% because of the restraining order.
contacts.quote: because I had the restraining order and because I did everything to get him out of the house and this was not my doing, that they would cover me a hundred percent.
contacts.what_happened_next: Rented them a house near her work.

contacts.what_institution_did: Ordered a 730 evaluation and allowed visitation monitored by his parents.
contacts.quote: Eventually we had to get a 730 evaluation ordered by the court.
contacts.what_happened_next: Monitored visitation by his parents.

contacts.what_institution_did: He was convicted of felony arson, breaking and entering and vandalism; one year of 'pay and stay' jail (nights only) and three years' probation.
contacts.quote: Ultimately, he was convicted of felony arson, breaking an entering and vandalism for all of that.
contacts.what_happened_next: She gave a victim impact statement; felt the sentence 'so unfair'.
contacts.notes: Conviction coded believed_and_acted; she considered the night-only jail sentence lenient.

contacts.when: after his parents took the boys out of the county
contacts.what_institution_did: Judge terminated visitation.
contacts.quote: So we called him into court and the judge terminated visitation.
contacts.what_happened_next: Later stepped back up to supervised then every-other-weekend visitation.

contacts.what_institution_did: Judge said in court he questioned her judgment for dropping the first restraining order.
contacts.quote: that after the arson, he said, I have a lot of respect for mom, but one thing that I don't is that she dropped the restraining order. I questioned mom's judgment.
contacts.what_happened_next: It 'stuck with' her and made her feel responsible.

persons.outcome_quote: This is not the person who was strung out on meth and threatening my life. This is a very different person in front of me.
persons.notes: Harm ended with the arson arrest, prosecution and court-controlled visitation; she also did substantial documentation work on her private divorce attorney's advice (private attorney not coded as an institution). Judge's reprimand for dropping the first order coded as blame (harmed_by_institution_ever true). A deputy also informally told her of his DUI/meth arrest. Later supervised visitation and co-parenting; she says he has done the work.

persons.decisive_work_quote: So we called him into court and the judge terminated visitation.
persons.name: [unnamed] Amelia's oldest son
persons.harm: Taken from daycare at about age three by his father, who was on methamphetamine, placed unrestrained in a car driven erratically, and used to extort $5,000 from his mother.
persons.perpetrator_role: his father (Amelia's ex-husband)

contacts.what_institution_did: Dispatched a helicopter to search for the car.
contacts.quote: I told that to the police and they dispatched a helicopter to try to find the car.
contacts.what_happened_next: Father brought him home around midnight; police did not find them.

contacts.institution: courthouse (ex parte restraining order) and sheriff's service
contacts.what_was_asked: remove the father from the home
contacts.what_institution_did: Order granted and served that night; father removed.
contacts.quote: He said, this is a restraining order. You need to vacate the premises immediately.
contacts.what_happened_next: Father later committed arson and was arrested.

contacts.when: after the arson and later violation
contacts.what_institution_did: Ordered a 730 evaluation, monitored visitation, and terminated visitation after the boys were taken out of county.
contacts.quote: So we called him into court and the judge terminated visitation.
contacts.what_happened_next: Visitation later rebuilt in supervised steps.

persons.outcome_quote: What I've told him is that daddy was making decisions that were scary, that weren't safe for him to be around them or to be around me.
persons.notes: The abduction itself ended when the father returned him, not through police; subsequent court orders controlled access. Mother acted for him in all contacts. Younger brother listed in others_mentioned.

quotes.quote: Did you see this as sexual abuse at the time? No. I literally thought of it as my job.
I think that our role in the church and the expectations that the church puts on women made it easier for me to accept the role that he wanted me to play.

persons.name: Odessa
persons.harm: Repeatedly coerced and guilt-tripped into prolonged painful sex that injured her, including sexual touching while she was asleep, plus deception, emotional withdrawal and financial draining by her youth-pastor husband.
persons.perpetrator_role: her husband, a youth pastor

contacts.what_institution_did: Told her to refrain from sex for a while after she was injured.
contacts.quote: there was a few times where I did get pretty decently injured and I was told by my doctor that I needed to reframe from having sex for a while.
contacts.what_happened_next: She describes this period as her 'escape' from painful sex.
contacts.notes: Unclear whether the doctor understood the injuries came from coerced sex.

contacts.when: six months pregnant, after he announced he was leaving
contacts.what_institution_did: OB hospitalised her for psychiatric evaluation; staff repeatedly asked if she was safe and offered security; she reassured them; they set her up with a therapist and medication.
contacts.quote: I had so many people asking me if I was safe, if I needed an out, if I needed him to leave, if I needed security to help.
contacts.what_happened_next: Discharged with a therapist she liked and medication.
contacts.notes: Staff offered help that she declined; coded acted_partly.

contacts.what_was_asked: space to explain how she felt about their sex life
contacts.what_institution_did: Told her that to help him with his porn addiction she must become 'his new drug', giving him sexual access whenever he wanted.
contacts.quote: She looked at me and said, Odessa, if you want to help him get through this addiction, you're going to have to become his new drug, his new addiction.
contacts.what_happened_next: She agreed out of fear of losing the marriage; her later therapist called it 'enabling your abuser'.
contacts.notes: Placing responsibility on her for his conduct and endangering her; also arguably protected the abuser.

contacts.what_institution_did: Validated her and named the earlier therapist's advice as enabling abuse.
contacts.quote: she was like, your therapist was enabling your abuser.
contacts.what_happened_next: Ongoing therapy.

persons.outcome_quote: We tolerate each other. I'm not going to say it's good.
persons.notes: The marriage ended because he left/she separated, not through any institution; she hired a private lawyer for divorce and co-parenting (not coded). Second witness: the youth student's question 'does he guilt trip you when you don't want to have sex too?' corroborates the pattern; sister reacted to the account. Outcome harmed_by_institution because the couples therapist's response is the only institutional response shown to have acted on the harm and no protection followed; a later therapist validated her.

persons.name: Madison
persons.harm: Groomed from age 16 by her youth pastor (Snapchat streaks, late-night texts), who began a sexual affair with her when she was about 19.
persons.perpetrator_role: her youth pastor (Odessa's husband)

contacts.institution: the church's lead pastor and elders
contacts.when: when she was a minor in the youth group
contacts.what_institution_did: Pulled the youth pastor aside and told him to have another person in the car when driving female students home; the concern was framed around her intentions.
contacts.quote: It always seemed like everybody was expecting Madison to do something, but no one expected [perpetrator].
contacts.what_happened_next: The relationship continued and later became sexual.
contacts.notes: Elders also pulled him aside; unclear whether the church understood this as grooming. Odessa says 'we really truly did believe that Madison was the problem'.

persons.outcome_quote: After a few weeks, it came out that they were officially back together, Madison and [perpetrator].
persons.notes: Her story is told only through Odessa and the youth student. Odessa calls her 'also a victim'. No report to any institution of the grooming is described.

quotes.quote: I was absolutely terrified because I still remember that line that his ID says that he's a woman. And because it says he's a woman that cops aren't going to give him the same amount of stress as if he was a bit.
I knew in my heart of heart that if I told anyone they would tell me to run, but it felt so good to be in that situation and to feel so seen and to feel so cared for that I didn't tell anyone.

persons.decisive_work_quote: I couldn't let there be no records. There needed to be a record.
persons.time_to_first_effective_action: about five days from calling the shelter
persons.name: Natalia (long-distance boyfriend)
persons.harm: Secretly filmed during sex without consent, controlled and intimidated during a visit, then harassed with spoofed calls, texts, threats to show up and unwanted deliveries by a long-distance partner.
persons.perpetrator_role: her long-distance boyfriend

contacts.what_institution_did: Advocate validated her and connected her to a local shelter and legal aid.
contacts.quote: She connected me into the local shelter and she connected me to some type of legal aid.
contacts.what_happened_next: Shelter connected her to a legal fellow.

contacts.institution: local shelter and legal-aid fellow (supervised attorney)
contacts.what_institution_did: Prepared and filed an emergency restraining order and later represented her in court and rejected the settlement push.
contacts.quote: We did the restraining order together and we filed an emergency restraining order.
contacts.what_happened_next: Order approved within about five days.

contacts.when: about five days after calling the shelter
contacts.what_institution_did: Judge approved an emergency restraining order.
contacts.quote: Within about five days from calling the shelter to speaking to the fellow to getting the paperwork filed, the judge approved an emergency restraining order, but then I had to get it to him.
contacts.what_happened_next: She had to find his address herself.

contacts.when: after she found his mother's address
contacts.what_institution_did: Served him via his mother's address; he picked it up at the station.
contacts.quote: So the sheriff served him with the emergency restraining order and they made court.
contacts.what_happened_next: Deliveries stopped.

contacts.what_institution_did: Judge reviewed her screenshots, rejected his excuses and granted a six-month protection order.
contacts.quote: the judge didn't buy it. And I am grateful that the judge didn't buy it, but then I'm also not grateful because they only granted me a six month protection order against him.
contacts.what_happened_next: No contact since the hearing.
contacts.notes: She felt six months was short given his multiple prior DV restraining orders.

persons.outcome_quote: But I haven't heard from him since that last court case. And I am grateful.
persons.notes: She gathered and organised screenshots, located his address through a paid background search, found his prior DV restraining orders and jail record, and refused a settlement that would have left no record. A friend suggested the hotline. She also hesitated over involving police against a Black trans man.

persons.name: Natalia (former partner)
persons.harm: Physical abuse by an earlier partner who hit her and repeatedly kicked her out; she says he caused her PTSD.
persons.perpetrator_role: her former partner

contacts.what_institution_did: Provided therapy and trauma counselling; no further detail.
contacts.quote: I had been through hell and back with [perpetrator]. I had gone to therapy and had gone to a trauma counselor

persons.outcome_quote: I left [perpetrator] with whatever I could fit in my car and I drove in the middle of the night.
persons.notes: Mentioned as background; she escaped by fleeing to her grandmother. The later partner says she was hit by this former partner (s13-e6 @ 23:03). She also describes herself as a rape survivor without detail.

quotes.quote: And I begin to become scared. And I think that I have dissociative identity disorder.

persons.name: Ruksana
persons.harm: For about three years her email and social media were hijacked to send threats, fake relapse notices and pro-Muslim-Brotherhood posts in her name by an unidentified, organised group, isolating her and leading her family to fear she had been radicalised.
persons.perpetrator_role: unidentified hackers/impersonators (she suspects acquaintances met through AA and a married man she was involved with)

contacts.when: when she discovered the Facebook posts
contacts.what_institution_did: Concluded someone was watching her and advised her to leave the city and stay with family.
contacts.quote: My therapist was like, you need to leave the city. You need to go home to stay with your family for a period of time.
contacts.what_happened_next: She moved back to her parents in the Midwest.

contacts.when: after the posts came to light
contacts.what_institution_did: Sheikh was asked to check whether she had been 'programmed' and to deprogram her.
contacts.quote: They took me to the mosque. I had to talk to a shake to see if I had been programmed or see if he could deprogram me.
contacts.what_happened_next: Her parents never apologised.
contacts.notes: Treated as the suspected wrongdoer rather than the victim; the response is shown via the parents' request.

contacts.what_was_asked: she half expected to turn herself in
contacts.what_institution_did: Detective said she was hacked, not a terrorist, and worked with her through IP addresses and emails, contacting everyone on her list.
contacts.quote: And as I started explaining my case to the detective, he was like, absolutely not. You're not a terrorist. Totally not. Your shit got hacked.
contacts.what_happened_next: They traced IPs to Amsterdam, Nigeria and government addresses.
contacts.notes: He also questioned how she could have believed the 'shaman' as 'a grown woman'.

contacts.when: after the IP trail showed government addresses
contacts.what_institution_did: Abruptly stopped helping, told her to change her name and said she was at fault for not protecting herself.
contacts.quote: And then he said that I was the one at fault because I didn't protect myself.
contacts.what_happened_next: She changed her name and moved.
contacts.notes: Also told her chasing it would cost a lot of money.

contacts.what_institution_did: Recovery was a 'fiasco'; she had to prove she was not the person posting.
contacts.quote: It was such a fiasco to have to prove to yourself that you're not that person or that your account has been hacked.
contacts.what_happened_next: Someone was actively changing passwords in real time.
contacts.notes: Outcome of the request not stated.

persons.outcome_quote: So there was really no resolution.
persons.notes: Perpetrator never identified. Second witnesses: sponsor showed her a fake email; cousin saw the posts; detective's calls confirmed recipients got threatening emails. A prior abusive boyfriend is mentioned only in passing (others_mentioned).

quotes.quote: I should have called the cops, but I didn't. I was like, you know what, this is just another one of those bad guys that you ran into.
I was scared to call the cops because cops are scary.

persons.name: Sage
persons.harm: Deceived by a con man using a false identity (with hired actors as 'family'), slammed into a wall and pushed toward her bed for sex, then stalked: attempted break-ins, notes left inside her gated complex, and a tracker on her phone.
persons.perpetrator_role: a man she dated from a dating app, using an alias

contacts.what_institution_did: Ignored the problems she raised.
contacts.quote: As problems started coming up and I shared them with some of the girls, I wasn't supported the way I thought I would be. If anything they ignored it.

contacts.what_institution_did: Did nothing.
contacts.quote: And so I reported that and the complex didn't do anything about it. They were like, okay, whatever.
contacts.what_happened_next: A second attempt followed.

contacts.what_institution_did: Told her they could not help and to call police.
contacts.quote: they literally were like, we can't do anything for you. You just need to call the cops.
contacts.what_happened_next: She called police.

contacts.what_institution_did: Identified his real name and record, scanned the notes, ran tests on her car and found he was tracking her phone; could not arrest.
contacts.quote: the one detective, turns his little computer and he's like, is this the guy you were dating?
contacts.what_happened_next: No arrest; she says 'the cops weren't able to do anything'.

contacts.what_institution_did: Refused: she was told another encounter was required.
contacts.quote: I asked for a restraining order and I was not allowed to get one. I tried multiple ways.
contacts.what_happened_next: Paperwork ready in case he appears again.

contacts.what_institution_did: Provided counselling, had her document red flags and also tried to get the order.
contacts.quote: Victim services tried to get it for me as well.
contacts.what_happened_next: She credits the counselling with helping her feel safer.

contacts.when: after police revealed he was a con man
contacts.what_institution_did: Did not care or support her; at Easter the next year he was told to leave.
contacts.quote: They didn't care, no one surrounded me.
contacts.what_happened_next: At Easter he showed up and 'was told to leave'.

contacts.what_institution_did: Supportive.
contacts.quote: My work boss was really there for me.

contacts.when: after he appeared at church at Easter
contacts.what_institution_did: Noted; no response described.
contacts.quote: I even reported it to the cops that he showed up at my church for Easter.
contacts.what_happened_next: He has not been caught.

persons.outcome_quote: And yeah, the cops weren't able to do anything. They weren't necessarily helpful.
persons.notes: She moved twice and now feels safer after counselling; he remains at large. Friend heard the wall/bed incident by phone. Dating app not shown to have been notified.

persons.decisive_work_quote: He was suspicious of the baby that she brought in, me. One reason is he thought it was weird that the baby on TV, baby Whitney, and the baby she was passing off as her own, both had a full head of hair with a curl on top.
persons.name: Whitney
persons.harm: Abducted from the hospital nursery as a one-day-old newborn by a stranger posing as a nurse and kept for 11 days.
persons.perpetrator_role: a 19-year-old stranger who faked a pregnancy

contacts.what_institution_did: Called a Code Pink and searched, but administrators waited about an hour to call authorities while holding a senior-staff meeting over likely lawsuit exposure.
contacts.quote: They decided to call an emergency board meeting or some type of meeting with their senior staff
contacts.what_happened_next: Authorities alerted around 1 a.m., about two hours after the abduction.

contacts.what_institution_did: Took the case (police transferred it to the FBI), ran daily press appeals and a tip line, and acted on a tip to recover her in Butler, Missouri.
contacts.quote: The FBI notified my parents on July 1st, 1990 at 1.30 a.m. They knocked on my parents' door, told them that they think they'd found me in Butler, Missouri.
contacts.what_happened_next: Kidnapper confessed and was arrested.

contacts.what_institution_did: Took her to the local hospital, where she was identified and found healthy.
contacts.quote: The social worker came to pick me up and took me to the local hospital there.
contacts.what_happened_next: Reunited with parents July 1.

contacts.what_institution_did: Kidnapper pleaded guilty to federal kidnapping; sentenced to five years plus three years' probation with mental-health care.
contacts.quote: She was sentenced to five years in prison or 60 months and three years probation with further mental care after her release.
contacts.what_happened_next: Parents 'very unhappy' with the sentence.
contacts.notes: Contrasted by the parents with a 20-year sentence for a Black man for car theft the same week.

persons.outcome_quote: I was very lucky. I was very lucky that my kidnapper did take good care of me.
persons.notes: Decisive work is genuinely mixed: a Hardee's manager recognised her from the FBI-orchestrated TV coverage and was motivated by her grandfather's reward; coded journalists_podcast_or_virality because the broadcast publicity is what produced the tip, with the FBI's media strategy and the family's reward as contributors (institution would also be defensible). An archival news clip of the mother's appeal is played on air; episode notes cite news archives. Parents (as third parties) could not sue the hospital; she chose not to sue by 19. The kidnapper's name is given on air but omitted here.

persons.decisive_work_quote: That was one characteristic of me that helped identify me was my hair. and the curl on top.
persons.name: Teresa (Whitney's mother)
persons.harm: Her one-day-old daughter was taken from the hospital nursery; she spent 11 days not knowing if her baby would return, appearing on live TV 36 hours postpartum.
persons.perpetrator_role: a stranger who kidnapped her newborn

contacts.what_institution_did: Delayed about an hour in calling authorities while senior staff met over lawsuit exposure.
contacts.quote: They had a potential lawsuit on their hands and they made a major mistake in their security and keeping their babies safe in their hospital.

contacts.what_institution_did: Coached daily appeals to the kidnapper and recovered the baby in 11 days.
contacts.quote: The FBI came to my parents' room in the early hours of June 21st, and they explained the typical process for families after their child goes missing.
contacts.what_happened_next: Baby recovered July 1.

contacts.what_institution_did: Five-year sentence after guilty plea.
contacts.quote: They were very unhappy with it because five years is not a long time.
contacts.what_happened_next: They could not sue the hospital as third parties.

contacts.what_institution_did: Waived the birth costs and provided free therapy; the head nurse had acted as her full-time nurse during the search.
contacts.quote: The hospital compensated my birth. They didn't have to pay for that. So there's that. They did provide free therapy for them after I came home, which helped.
contacts.what_happened_next: Parents later divorced.

persons.outcome_quote: it's not every day that a kidnapped 11-day-old baby is found and returned home safely and in good health.
persons.notes: Told by her daughter; she did not speak on the show except in an archival news clip. Same decisive-work caveat as P09.

persons.decisive_work_quote: we ended up getting picked up by the cops.
persons.time_to_first_effective_action: about two days after running away
persons.name: Iris
persons.harm: At 13, manipulated by a close friend who invented online 'friends' and an abuse story, pushed her into pill-taking and self-harm games, theft and running away across the state in winter.
persons.perpetrator_role: her best friend from middle school

contacts.when: the morning after they ran away
contacts.what_institution_did: Went on high alert and interviewed classmates.
contacts.quote: They went into high alert at the school and started pulling people out and interviewing all of our friends at school
contacts.what_happened_next: Parents traced them to a friend's house but they hid.

contacts.when: about two days after they ran away
contacts.what_institution_did: Picked them up at a convenience store, separated them, saw through their fake names and contacted the parents.
contacts.quote: At that point, we ended up getting picked up by the cops. It was a huge relief with that.

coder_notes: All 12 chunk files read in full to their last lines. Unassigned INDEX read; three episodes opened (none continue an S13 story); the others were judged from the index to be general data-point episodes or unrelated stories. Private attorneys (Amelia's divorce lawyer, Birdie's attorneys, Odessa's divorce lawyer, the crematory employee's lawyer, Sadie's mother's law firm) are not coded as institutions. Two different perpetrators in Grace's and Gianna's stories share the same pseudonym on the show. Perpetrator names replaced by [perpetrator] in quotations; names of non-harmed people avoided. Decisive-work codes for Whitney/Teresa (publicity vs FBI) and Claire (her evidence vs school/other victim) are judgement calls noted in each record. Some single-story episodes contain several people whose harms are told only secondhand; those are low confidence.
